rationale: The assistant correctly latched onto the new drawer unit as the key clue and steered toward overheat protection from restricted ventilation, with power isolation advised before any under-hob check and a sensible hand-off to an engineer when the customer refused to look underneath. It respected the customer's refusals and stayed hedged ('it is likely', 'may also be struggling or failed'). Weaknesses: it never probed the loud fan or asked the customer to capture the fleeting code (e.g. phone video), the model-number panel was an irrelevant 'suitable replacement' card with door-based location hints that make no sense for a hob, and it asked the customer to look under the hob a second time after they had declined, though for a different purpose. No parts were recommended and no unsafe instructions given.
